title: Career Roadmap · Graphic Designer
summary: A Graphic Designer creates visual content to communicate ideas, promote products, strengthen brands and improve audience engagement. Typical work includes designing social media creatives, posters, advertisements, brochures, presentations, packaging, logos and digital campaign assets.

about.label: Primary sectors
about.text: Advertising, branding, digital marketing, media, publishing, e-commerce

about.label: Work environment
about.text: Design studios, agencies, corporate marketing teams, production houses and freelance settings

blocks.text: A Graphic Designer creates visual content to communicate ideas, promote products, strengthen brands and improve audience engagement. Typical work includes designing social media creatives, posters, advertisements, brochures, presentations, packaging, logos and digital campaign assets.

Graphic designers combine visual communication, typography, colour theory, layout, image editing and creative problem-solving. They also interpret client briefs, follow brand guidelines, prepare design files and revise their work based on feedback.
This career is suitable for students who enjoy visual creativity, digital tools, storytelling and turning ideas into clear, attractive designs.

rows.text: Create social media posts, banners, simple layouts and design variations
Manage design briefs, develop campaign assets and maintain brand consistency
Lead visual concepts, mentor juniors and handle complex design projects
Art Director / Creative Lead / Design Manager
Guide visual strategy, oversee design teams and maintain creative quality

blocks.text: Progression depends on portfolio quality, visual judgement, communication, reliability and the complexity of projects handled.
The following plan assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt it to the actual duration and curriculum of the institution.
Year 1
Foundation
Develop visual design fundamentals

items.text: Learn colour theory, composition, contrast, balance and visual hierarchy.
Study typography, font pairing, readability and spacing.
Practise grids, alignment, white space and layout principles.
Learn basic photo editing, cropping, masking and image correction.
Understand raster versus vector graphics, resolution and file formats.
Recreate simple layouts for learning purposes, then create original designs.
Explore tools such as Canva, Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator or equivalent software.

blocks.text: Year 2
Specialisation
Build professional design capability

items.text: Create social media campaigns, posters, brochures and advertising creatives.
Learn logo development, brand identity and visual systems.
Practise vector illustration, image compositing and retouching.
Understand print specifications, bleed, colour modes and export settings.
Learn digital design dimensions and asset preparation for websites and mobile screens.
Develop skills in presenting concepts and incorporating feedback.
Explore motion graphics and basic animation if relevant to the chosen specialisation.

blocks.text: Year 3
Job readiness
Prepare a professional portfolio

items.text: Develop complete branding projects from brief to final deliverables.
Create a campaign with multiple coordinated social media and advertising assets.
Learn design handoff, file organisation, naming conventions and version control.
Practise responding to client briefs, estimating effort and meeting deadlines.
Complete an internship with a design studio, advertising agency, brand or marketing team.
Build a portfolio website or PDF casebook featuring selected projects and design rationale.
Learn responsible AI-assisted design workflows, licensing and asset attribution.

blocks.text: Students do not need to master every tool before applying for jobs. Start with a raster editor, a vector design tool and a simple portfolio workflow; add specialist tools according to the roles being targeted.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Brand identity system
Create a fictional brand with a logo, colour palette, typography system, business card and one-page brand guideline. Explain the audience and the design decisions behind the identity.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Social media campaign
Design a coordinated set of 8–10 posts for a fictional product launch. Keep typography, colours and visual style consistent while adapting the layout to different messages.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Packaging design
Create a package label or box design with product information, brand elements and an appropriate layout. Include a mock-up and a print-ready file specification sheet.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Editorial layout
Design a short digital magazine or brochure using grids, headings, images, captions and consistent typography. Demonstrate readable information hierarchy.

blocks.label: Project 5
blocks.text: Advertising campaign
Develop a campaign for a fictional service with a poster, web banner, social media ad and presentation slide. Explain the message, intended audience and visual strategy.

For each project, include the brief, target audience, initial concepts, final designs and a short explanation of key decisions. Use original assets or resources with appropriate licences, and clearly identify fictional work.

blocks.text: Select 5–8 strong projects rather than including every practice exercise. Show a range of work, consistent execution and the ability to explain your design decisions.

Certifications are supplementary. For most entry-level graphic design roles, employers will closely assess the quality and relevance of your portfolio.
After gaining experience, a Graphic Designer can specialise in:

blocks.label: Brand identity design
blocks.text: Logos, typography, brand systems and guidelines.

blocks.label: Social media design
blocks.text: Campaign assets and platform-specific graphics.

blocks.label: Advertising design

blocks.label: Packaging design
blocks.text: Product labels, packaging layouts and production-ready artwork.

blocks.label: Editorial design
blocks.text: Magazines, brochures, reports and publications.

blocks.label: Motion graphics
blocks.text: Animated typography, explainers and campaign visuals.

blocks.label: Digital product graphics
blocks.text: Icons, illustrations and visual assets for websites and apps.

blocks.label: Art direction

blocks.text: AI can accelerate ideation and production, but it does not replace strong composition, typography, visual judgement or an understanding of the client's brief. Check the usage rights and authenticity of assets before commercial use.

By the end of the B.Voc programme, the student should aim to have:

items.text: A strong understanding of typography, colour, composition and layout.
Practical skills in at least one raster editor and one vector design tool.
Experience creating brand identities and digital marketing creatives.
Basic knowledge of print production and digital export specifications.
Five to eight well-presented portfolio projects.
The ability to interpret a brief and explain design decisions.
An internship or experience working on realistic project briefs.
Knowledge of asset licensing, attribution and responsible AI-assisted workflows.

blocks.text: Final recommendation

For a Graphic Designer role, prioritise visual fundamentals, tool proficiency and a focused portfolio. Build original projects that demonstrate both creative thinking and accurate execution. A smaller portfolio of well-resolved, clearly explained work is generally more persuasive than a large collection of repetitive designs.
